newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany on course for EMU, Waigel says.
newsitem.headline: Germany on course for EMU, Waigel says.

text.p: Germany is on course to cut its borrowing sufficiently this year to qualify for European monetary union (EMU) in 1999, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday.

Waigel told parliament that, despite rising unemployment, Bonn would still hit its target cutting the budget deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP -- below the three percent ceiling set by the Maastricht treaty.
"Latest developments give me no reason to depart from this forecast," Waigel said in remarks prepared for a debate on EMU called by the opposition Greens.

Saying that investment and business confidence were rising, and the European Union council of finance ministers had backed his view, Waigel added: "The growth forecast of 2-1/2 percent in real terms is realistic."
Waigel also sought to dampen speculation that European leaders would go soft on the Maastricht criteria when they meet in early 1998 to decide which countries can join EMU in 1999.
"The government will observe a 'strict and narrow' interpretation of the convergence criteria at this examination of convergence," Waigel said.
Waigel said that meant that, as the treaty states, "a high degree of sustained convergence is achieved".
"We are sticking to the rules set by the treaty, from which comes my repeated assertion: Convergence determines the timetable," he said.
Waigel dismissed comments on a possible delay to the start of EMU as "pure speculation" as long as final economic data for this year are not available.
